newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot rejects criticism of Boeing choice.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot rejects criticism of Boeing choice.

text.p: Aeroflot on Friday rejected complaints by Russian plane makers about its recent decision to buy 10 Boeing medium range jets, and said the deal was good for the Russian flag carrier.
Chief Executive Yevgeny Shaposhnikov told a news conference the acquisition of the 10 737-400 jets would not hurt Russian aviation companies.
"The purchase of these jets will not damage Russian plane-makers, but this step will help Aeroflot improve its activities on the international market," he said.
"I do not see a conflict between Aeroflot and Russian plane manufacturers."

Earlier this month the premier of Russia's autonomous region of Tatarstan denounced Aeroflot Russian International Airlines's decision to buy Boeing planes in 1997 and 1998, saying it would hurt the crisis-ridden Russian aviation industry.
Russian plane-maker Tupolev is based in the Tatarstan capital of Kazan.
Aeroflot sources said the total cost of the 10 planes could be around $350 million.
Shaposhnikov refused to say how Aeroflot would fund the purchase, saying the deal had not yet been signed.
Aeroflot's head of long-range aircraft Vladimir Barilov said Russian aviation plants do not now produce efficient planes.
"Ten Western-made aircraft which we operated among our 100 plane fleet accounted for 70 percent of our passenger volume in 1995," he said.
One Boeing 767 was in flight 16 hours a day compared with 5.4 hours for a Russian-made Ilyushin-96-300 jet, he said.
Aeroflot chief engineer Vladimir Klimenko said the engines of the Russian-made Tupolev-204 needed to be improved.
"To improve the Tupolev-214 (an upgraded version of the 204) one year of test flights are needed costing billion of roubles," he said.
"We cannot wait for these planes," Shaposhnikov said, adding Aeroflot had chosen the Boeings because there were no Russian competitors in its class.
